newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB forecast drop in world wheat prices in '97/98.
newsitem.headline: CWB forecast drop in world wheat prices in '97/98.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board on Monday forecast a drop of up to C$36.00 per tonne in world wheat prices in the marketing year 1997/98 (August/July) compared with the current marketing year.
"The new forecasts for wheat and barley indicate a significant drop from expected returns for 1996/97," the CWB said in a statement.

Benchmark no 1. Canada western red spring wheat was forecast in the C$160 to C$190.00 per tonne range in-store Vancouver or St. Lawrence for 1997/98 compared to C$193.00 to C$208.00 in last month's CWB world price estimate for 1996/97.
"Early estimates indicate lower wheat returns relative to 1996/97, due largely to a significant increase in ending stocks of the major exporters," CWB said.
"Although it is still early, the EU (European Union) and U.S. winter wheat crops are in good condition," the board added, noting low wheat stocks should keep prices volatile.

The benchmark no.1 Canada western amber durum wheat was forecast to range in 1997/98 between C$175.00 to C$205.00 per tonne, compared to last month's 1996/97 estimate of C$204.00 to C$224.00 per tonne.

"Although regions of North Africa remain relatively dry, rains in early February have eased some of the crop stress. North Africa's durum production, which will be harvested in May/June, will depend heavily on rainfall over the next month," the CWB said.
Benchmark no.1 Canada western feed barley was forecast at between C$110 to C$140 per tonne in 1997/98 versus last month's 1996/97 estimated range of C$143 to C$158 per tonne.

"European Union barley carryout estimates for 1996/97 are approximately 10 million tonnes, versus 4.3 million at the end of 1995/96. The EU winter barley crop is in good condition and current projections indicate barley production similar to 1996/97," CWB said.
Special select Canada western two-row malt barley was forecast at C$165 to C$195 in 1997/98 compared to last month's estimate of C$223 to C$233 in 1996/97.
Special select Canada western six-row malt barley was forecast to range between C$130 to C$160 per tonne in 1997/98, versus last month's estimate of C$186 to C$196 in 1996/97.
CWB attributed the expected decline in malt barley prices partly to good quality Australian barley crops.
